24: const AFTER_HELP: &str = help_section!("after help", "tr.md");
25: const USAGE: &str = help_usage!("tr.md");
26: 
27: mod options {
28:     pub const COMPLEMENT: &str = "complement";
29:     pub const DELETE: &str = "delete";
30:     pub const SQUEEZE: &str = "squeeze-repeats";
31:     pub const TRUNCATE_SET1: &str = "truncate-set1";
32:     pub const SETS: &str = "sets";
33: }

35: #[uucore::main]
36: pub fn uumain(args: impl uucore::Args) -> UResult<()> {
37:     let matches = uu_app().after_help(AFTER_HELP).try_get_matches_from(args)?;
38: 
39:     let delete_flag = matches.get_flag(options::DELETE);
40:     let complement_flag = matches.get_flag(options::COMPLEMENT);
41:     let squeeze_flag = matches.get_flag(options::SQUEEZE);
42:     let truncate_set1_flag = matches.get_flag(options::TRUNCATE_SET1);
43: 
44:     // Ultimately this should be OsString, but we might want to wait for the
45:     // pattern API on OsStr
46:     let sets: Vec<_> = matches
47:         .get_many::<OsString>(options::SETS)
48:         .into_iter()
49:         .flatten()
50:         .map(ToOwned::to_owned)
51:         .collect();
52: 
53:     let sets_len = sets.len();
54:     check_operand_count(delete_flag, squeeze_flag, &sets)?;
55: 
56:     if let Some(first) = sets.first() {
57:         let slice = os_str_as_bytes(first)?;
58: 
59:         let mut iter = slice.iter();
60: 
61:         if let Some(b'\\') = iter.next_back() {
62:             match iter.next_back() {
63:                 Some(b'\\') => {
64:                     // The trailing backslash has a backslash preceding it, so it is properly escaped
65:                 }
66:                 _ => {
67:                     // The trailing backslash has a non-backslash character before it OR is the only character in the
68:                     // string, so the warning applies
69:                     show!(USimpleError::new(
70:                         0,
71:                         "warning: an unescaped backslash at end of string is not portable"
72:                     ));
73:                 }
74:             }
75:         }
76:     }
77: 
78:     let stdin = stdin();
79:     let mut locked_stdin = stdin.lock();
80:     let stdout = stdout();
81:     let locked_stdout = stdout.lock();
82:     let mut buffered_stdout = BufWriter::new(locked_stdout);
83: 
84:     // According to the man page: translating only happens if deleting or if a second set is given
85:     let translating = !delete_flag && sets.len() > 1;
86:     let mut sets_iter = sets.iter().map(|c| c.as_os_str());
87:     let set1_os = sets_iter.next().unwrap_or_default();
88:     let set2_os = sets_iter.next().unwrap_or_default();
89: 
90:     #[cfg(unix)]
91:     let set1_bytes: &[u8] = {
92:         use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
93:         set1_os.as_bytes()
94:     };
95:     #[cfg(not(unix))]
96:     let set1_bytes: &[u8] = match set1_os.to_str() {
97:         Some(text) => text.as_bytes(),
98:         None => {
99:             return Err(UUsageError::new(
100:                 1,
101:                 "invalid UTF-8 was detected in one or more arguments",
102:             ));
103:         }
104:     };
105: 
106:     #[cfg(unix)]
107:     let set2_bytes: &[u8] = {
108:         use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
109:         set2_os.as_bytes()
110:     };
111:     #[cfg(not(unix))]
112:     let set2_bytes: &[u8] = match set2_os.to_str() {
113:         Some(text) => text.as_bytes(),
114:         None => {
115:             return Err(UUsageError::new(
116:                 1,
117:                 "invalid UTF-8 was detected in one or more arguments",
118:             ));
119:         }
120:     };
121: 
122:     let (set1, set2) = Sequence::solve_set_characters(
123:         set1_bytes,
124:         set2_bytes,
125:         complement_flag,
126:         // if we are not translating then we don't truncate set1
127:         truncate_set1_flag && translating,
128:         translating,
129:     )?;
130: 
131:     // '*_op' are the operations that need to be applied, in order.
132:     let mut translator: Box<dyn SymbolTranslator> = if delete_flag {
133:         if squeeze_flag {
134:             let delete_op = DeleteOperation::new(set1);
135:             let squeeze_op = SqueezeOperation::new(set2);
136:             Box::new(delete_op.chain(squeeze_op))
137:         } else {
138:             Box::new(DeleteOperation::new(set1))
139:         }
140:     } else if squeeze_flag {
141:         if sets_len < 2 {
142:             Box::new(SqueezeOperation::new(set1))
143:         } else {
144:             let translate_op = TranslateOperation::new(set1, set2.clone())?;
145:             let squeeze_op = SqueezeOperation::new(set2);
146:             Box::new(translate_op.chain(squeeze_op))
147:         }
148:     } else {
149:         Box::new(TranslateOperation::new(set1, set2)?)
150:     };
151: 
152:     let mut input_buf = Vec::new();
153:     let mut output_buf = Vec::new();
154:     while locked_stdin
155:         .read_until(b'\n', &mut input_buf)
156:         .map_or(false, |length| length > 0)
157:     {
158:         let filtered = input_buf
159:             .iter()
160:             .filter_map(|current| translator.translate(*current));
161:         output_buf.extend(filtered);
162:         buffered_stdout.write_all(&output_buf).unwrap();
163:         input_buf.clear();
164:         output_buf.clear();
165:     }
166:     Ok(())
167: }

169: fn check_operand_count(
170:     delete_flag: bool,
171:     squeeze_flag: bool,
172:     sets: &[OsString],
173: ) -> UResult<()> {
174:     let sets_len = sets.len();
175: 
176:     if sets.is_empty() {
177:         return Err(UUsageError::new(1, "missing operand"));
178:     }
179: 
180:     if !(delete_flag || squeeze_flag) && sets_len < 2 {
181:         return Err(UUsageError::new(
182:             1,
183:             format!(
184:                 "missing operand after {}\nTwo strings must be given when translating.",
185:                 sets[0].quote()
186:             ),
187:         ));
188:     }
189: 
190:     if delete_flag & squeeze_flag && sets_len < 2 {
191:         return Err(UUsageError::new(
192:             1,
193:             format!(
194:                 "missing operand after {}\nTwo strings must be given when deleting and squeezing.",
195:                 sets[0].quote()
196:             ),
197:         ));
198:     }
199: 
200:     if sets_len > 1 {
201:         let start = "extra operand";
202:         if delete_flag && !squeeze_flag {
203:             let op = sets[1].quote();

208:                 )

210:                 format!("{} {}", start, op,)
211:             };

213:         }

215:             let op = sets[2].quote();
216:             let msg = format!("{} {}", start, op);
217:             return Err(UUsageError::new(1, msg));
218:         }
219:     }
220: 
221:     Ok(())
222: }

part.text:
Fixed `tr`’s trailing-backslash portability warning in `src/uu/tr/src/tr.rs`.

The check now counts the complete run of trailing backslashes and warns only when that count is odd. This correctly handles runs such as three or five backslashes, which were previously mistaken for escaped endings.

Validated in the supplied container:

- `cargo test --features tr --test tests tr::test_trailing_backslash`
- `cargo test --features tr --test tests tr::test_unescaped_backslash_warning_false_positive`
- `git diff --check`
